To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BM cell therapy improves left ventricular function and exercise tolerance in patients with acute anterior MI.
BM cell transplantation improves cardiac function and exercise tolerance in patients with MI.
the intracoronary infusion of autologous bone marrow cells (BM‐cells) in acute ST‐segment elevated myocardial infarctions patients improves the cardiac, autonomic and functional indexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of intramyocardial transplantation of autologous bone marrow cells (BMC) on the recovery of left ventricular function and the autonomic nervous system (ANS) in patients with acute anterior wall myocardial infarctions (AMI) treated with reperfusion therapy.
the use of stem cells in cardiac repair and regeneration.
the use of autologous bone marrow cells in the treatment of myocardial infarctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BM cell transplantation is not effective in the treatment of acute MI.
the BM cell therapy in acute MI patients improves cardiac function (LVEF, stroke volume, exercise stress SPECT), autonomic function (BRS, HRV), and functional status (6‐minute walk test).
BM cells have no significant effect on the cardiac and autonomic indexes and functional exercise capacity in acute anterior MI patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BM cell transplantation improves cardiac function and outcome, and the improvement of cardiac function is related to the increase of stroke volume, autonomic control, and exercise tolerance.
BM cells improve cardiac and autonomic indexes and functional exercise capacity in post‐MI.
the intracoronary infusion of autologous bone marrow cells improves cardiac function, autonomic function, and exercise capacity in patients with acute myocardial infarctions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intracoronary infusion of BM cells improves cardiac function and autonomic control, as well as exercise tolerance and functional class, and reduces infarct size in post‐acute MI patients.
intracoronary BM cell transplantation improves cardiac function, stroke volume, autonomic control, and functional indexes after acute anterior MI.
intracoronary infusion of autologous bone marrow cells in acute anterior myocardium infarction patients improved left ventricular ejections fraction and volumes, stroke volume, and autonomic control.
